note: Sample cuts bundled so a tester can try the tool without supplying footage. Five clips are 60-second excerpts of public-domain sponsored films from the Prelinger Archives at the Internet Archive; three are Creative Commons excerpts from Wikimedia Commons, carrying an attribution requirement recorded in its rights field. The cue sheets are illustrative sample documents written for these excerpts, not authoritative music rights data - see README.md in this directory.

samples.title: Century 21 Calling
samples.rights: Public domain (Prelinger Archives; Internet Archive public domain mark)
samples.blurb: Two teenagers tour the Seattle World's Fair. The densest clip here for signage: shopfront lettering, neon, exhibit branding and the Space Needle, plus a crowd of identifiable faces.
samples.exercises: Signage and trade marks read straight off the frame, an architectural work, background faces, and Bell System branding throughout.

samples.title: Design for Dreaming
samples.rights: Public domain (Prelinger Archives; Internet Archive public domain mark)
samples.blurb: The GM Motorama musical. A masked dancer, concept cars on turntables, and an orchestral number over the whole excerpt.
samples.exercises: A featured performer, motor vehicle designs and marques, and a music cue whose composer the cue sheet cannot name - so the publisher has to be researched.

samples.title: Duck and Cover
samples.rights: Public domain (Prelinger Archives; Internet Archive public domain mark)
samples.blurb: Bert the Turtle, animated, over the title song. The clearest illustration of a work being in the public domain while a character and a song inside it still have to be traced.
samples.exercises: An animated character, a named song with no publisher on the cue sheet, and a government work - three different answers to 'who owns this'.

samples.title: A Word to the Wives
samples.sponsor: American Gas Association and The Woman's Home Companion
samples.rights: Public domain (Prelinger Archives; Internet Archive public domain mark)
samples.blurb: Opens on a main title card crediting a real, named star. The performer question arrives before anything else in the frame does.
samples.exercises: A credited screen performer, a sponsoring magazine title, domestic appliances and packaged goods in shot.

samples.title: Chevrolet Sales Convention Musical
samples.rights: Public domain (Prelinger Archives; Internet Archive public domain mark)
samples.blurb: A full stage chorus number staged for a dealer convention. Dozens of performers, continuous music, and a painted backdrop.
samples.exercises: A crowd of performers rather than one, a wall-to-wall music cue, and scenic artwork - the case where nobody in frame is individually identifiable.

samples.title: Shibuya Scramble Crossing
samples.rights: CC BY 3.0 - Japan Travel Rec, via Wikimedia Commons. Attribution is required and travels with this clip. The licence is the uploader's assertion carried over from YouTube and is still awaiting Commons licence review; it is restated here, not independently determined by this project.
samples.blurb: A minute crossing Shibuya at street level. The only modern clip in the set, and the only one shot outside the United States - shop and station signage in two scripts, a wall of illuminated advertising, and a crowd nobody could individually clear.
samples.exercises: Living trade marks read straight off the frame - Uniqlo, H&M, Visa, Mastercard, Aeon, Gusto, Shibuya 109 - against holders who still trade, so research resolves to a named company rather than a lapsed estate. Also an advertising screen playing a commercial inside the shot, which needs its own clip licence; vehicle designs and readable plates; a Japanese territory on a report otherwise written for US rights; and no cue sheet at all, so the music path runs on the audio alone.

samples.title: Piccadilly Circus
samples.rights: CC BY 3.0 - Kauko Helavuo, via Wikimedia Commons. Attribution is required and travels with this clip; the author's copyright notice is burned into the picture and is retained deliberately, because the licence requires the notice to be kept. Licence reviewed on Commons. Restated here, not independently determined by this project.
samples.blurb: A minute standing in Piccadilly Circus. The curved advertising screen fills the frame with brands that all still trade, a public sculpture sits in the middle of the junction, and the crowd in front of it is unclearable.
samples.exercises: A wall of live trade marks at once - Coca-Cola, Samsung, Hyundai, McDonald's, Vogue, Gap, Boots - so de-duplication and per-work billing both get a workout. Also a sculpture in a public place, where the answer turns on freedom of panorama rather than on who owns the mark; a UK territory; vehicle liveries and bus-side advertising; and a visible copyright notice belonging to the clip itself.

samples.title: Street Orchestra Flash Mob
samples.rights: CC BY 3.0 - uploaded to Wikimedia Commons by Yojan Smith Chipana Sierra, licence reviewed there. Two cautions travel with this clip, and they are the reason it is included rather than a reason to rely on it. First, the picture carries a 'Rhapsody Philharmonic' credit that does not match the uploader, so the chain from performer to uploader is not established. Second, the music heard in it is a released cover recording, which no Creative Commons licence over the picture can grant. Both restated here, not independently determined by this project.
samples.blurb: A street orchestra playing a chart song to a crowd that has stopped to watch. The only sample whose music an acoustic search can actually name - and the only one whose own paperwork does not survive a second look.
samples.exercises: The two-sided music clearance, which no other sample reaches: a cover recording splits into a composition, needing a sync licence from the song's publishers, and a master, needing a licence from whoever owns this particular recording - and acoustic identification has to name the cue before either question can be put. There is no cue sheet, so the name has to come from the audio. Also performers working on camera, a crowd behind them, and a producer credit burned into the picture whose relationship to the uploaded licence is unclear: the clip is its own worked example of the gap it is meant to teach.
